# Source register

## AB01 / 160 acres: Township Road 564 and Range Road 211

Government of Alberta Regional Dashboard / published Undated live listing / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://regionaldashboard.alberta.ca/property/201504)

Supports: Listing identifies SE 23-56-21-W4, 160 acres, AG zoning and Sandhills Heavy Industrial Policy Area; reports a 240 kV AltaLink line 1.35 km away and estimated fibre availability. HTML map marker is 53.8663990960219, -113.001631865825.

Limit: Listing is evidence of a marketed candidate, not current availability, ownership, a survey, utility capacity or connection rights. Distances are straight-line estimates.

## AB02 / Large Load Projects

AESO / published Live page; guide posted 2026-06-12 / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.aeso.ca/grid/connecting-to-the-grid/large-load-projects/)

Supports: Phase 1 has allocated all 1,200 MW: GLDC 970 MW and Keephills Phase I 230 MW; other applications enter Phase 2.

Limit: No capacity allocated to this proposal; named projects are unrelated third parties.

## AB03 / Phase 2A Large Load Integration: BYOG Process

AESO / published 2026-09-08 latest dated stakeholder update inspected / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://aesoengage.aeso.ca/pre-engagement-phase-ii-large-load-integration)

Supports: September update says final BYOG process and materials are still being finalized and intake is expected in fall; earlier draft outcomes are explicitly not final.

Limit: This is the published page state inspected, not confirmation intake remains closed on every other AESO channel. Final ratios, qualifying generation, tethering and milestones need confirmation.

## AB04 / Guide to AESO Connection Requirements for Transmission-Connected Data Centres

AESO / published 2026-06-12 / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.aeso.ca/assets/Uploads/grid/Guide-to-AESO-Connection-Requirements-for-Transmission-Connected-Data-Centres.pdf)

Supports: Guide covers load dynamics, protection, backup synchronization, operational coordination and possible 10 MW/min point-of-connection ramp limits; its examples are illustrative.

Limit: Project requirements emerge from studies and binding agreements. This proposal has no validated dynamic model or approved ramp envelope.

## AB05 / Powering new pathways for data centres

Government of Alberta / published Royal assent 2025-12-11 / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.alberta.ca/powering-new-pathways-for-data-centres)

Supports: Bill 8 framework encourages own generation and cost-causation for transmission upgrades.

Limit: Policy direction does not establish approved project service, final tariff or an energization date.

## AB06 / Strathcona land use bylaw: zones and maps

Strathcona County / published Live consolidated page / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.strathcona.ca/council-county/bylaws-and-policies/land-use-bylaw/interactive-lub/part-1-interpretation/zones-and-maps/)

Supports: County distinguishes AG, Heavy Industrial Heartland (IHH), Medium Industrial Heartland (IMH), utilities and overlays; mapped zoning governs.

Limit: Does not determine a data-centre/generation use classification or rezone the candidate. Seek written interpretation and current parcel zoning certificate.

## AB07 / Rule 007: Facility Applications

Alberta Utilities Commission / published Effective 2025-11-06 / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.auc.ab.ca/rules/rule007/)

Supports: Current AUC facility application rule and forms cover thermal generation, transmission and substations.

Limit: Timing and hearing requirements are case-specific; none of this proposal has been filed.

## AB08 / Proposing a power plant application

Alberta Utilities Commission / published Live guidance / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.auc.ab.ca/proposing-a-power-plant-application/)

Supports: AUC guidance addresses facility applications, affected persons, Rule 012 noise and separate EPEA requirements for thermal plants above 1 MW.

Limit: General guidance; exact industrial, generation, pipeline and environmental approval boundaries require regulator and counsel confirmation.

## AB09 / Water legislation and guidelines

Government of Alberta / published Live guidance / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.alberta.ca/water-legislation-and-guidelines)

Supports: Water Act/EPEA framework includes diversion licences, activity approvals, wetlands, wastewater and stormwater guidance.

Limit: Dry cooling does not exempt site drainage, wetland disturbance, construction water or domestic supply from applicable requirements.

## AB10 / Technology Innovation and Emissions Reduction Regulation

Government of Alberta / published Includes December 2025 amendments / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.alberta.ca/technology-innovation-and-emissions-reduction-regulation)

Supports: TIER generally covers facilities emitting at least 100,000 tonnes CO2e per year; compliance is benchmark-based, not simply gross emissions times a headline tax.

Limit: Plant-specific treatment, benchmark, credits and compliance prices are unresolved; no assumed exemption or incentive.

## AB11 / Wartsila 31SG gas engine product technical data

Wartsila Energy / published Live product page / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.wartsila.com/energy/engine-power-plant-solutions/engine-power-plant-products/wartsila-31sg-gas-engine)

Supports: Manufacturer publishes 60 Hz units around 10.4–12.4 MW and heat rates around 6.9–7.1 GJ/MWh at specified reference conditions.

Limit: A technology reference, not a selected supplier, quote, delivery slot or site guarantee; auxiliaries, climate, emissions and fuel change net output.

## AB12 / Canadian Climate Normals 1991–2020

Environment and Climate Change Canada / published 1991–2020 dataset / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.climate.weather.gc.ca/climate_normals/index_e.html)

Supports: Official normals use composite stations with at least 15 years of observations; appropriate starting point for an hourly site weather study.

Limit: No hourly simulation or site design extremes extracted here. All design temperatures and PUE values in this proposal are assumptions, not values attributed to this page.

## AB14 / LDA26-0225: Edmonton Energy and Technology Park AI Data Centre Amendment

City of Edmonton / published 2026 live application consultation / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://engaged.edmonton.ca/eetpdatacentre)

Supports: City describes large AI data centres as allowed in the chemical-cluster zone but currently not allowed in the medium-industrial zone; an amendment is under consideration.

Limit: An application is not an approval. No specific available EETP parcel is secured or represented by this proposal.

## AB15 / Alberta tax overview: data centre levy

Government of Alberta, Treasury Board and Finance / published Effective 2026-01-01 per live page / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.alberta.ca/taxes-levies-overview)

Supports: Provincial overview says equipment levy effective January 1, 2026, up to 2%, with lower rates for projects supplying their own power and corporate-tax treatment.

Limit: Facility SPV versus tenant liability, rate formula and tax-credit realization need tax counsel. Exclusion of GPU CAPEX from this model is not a levy exemption.

## AB16 / Canada–Alberta Implementation Agreement

Prime Minister of Canada / published 2026-05-15 / accessed 2026-10-13

[Open source](https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/news/backgrounders/2026/05/15/implementation-agreement-canada-alberta-memorandum-understanding)

Supports: Agreement conditionally holds Clean Electricity Regulations in abeyance while the reference and possible appeals proceed; contemplates subsequent equivalency negotiations if upheld.

Limit: Does not guarantee permanent exemption or a 20-year plant operating entitlement. Read with current legislation, litigation and project-specific advice.
